chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Her retirement years: daughter's school and community work
summary: Her daughter's school troubles led her to the parents' association, after-school help for children and the Board of Education.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Okay, we've been off tape for quite awhile. We're coming back now into the chronological sequence now, which we're picking up at the time

of your retirement which was for something like twelve years, right?
So perhaps you can tell us a little bit about what you were doing during that time.

Well, as I mentioned before, you know, Paula, my daughter, was graduating from elementary school, and when I came off the road in '57 I wasn't well and I had an operation so I just sort of used this opportunity to stop. And as Paula was going into Junior High School I figured it was time for me to get involved with the Parents Association, etcetera. I have been a member of the Parents Association ever since she entered school but because of my schedule I couldn't really get involved. I was just a member, so to speak. But, Paula being a girl I figured, you know, maybe I should get involved, and she's getting older, a teenager, you know, your problems, and you got to start thinking seriously now of which direction she's going to go. So I joined the Parents Association and once I became involved I went in to see her teachers and I found out some things that I would otherwise have no way of knowing. About

how she was doing in school. What some of the problems were. And so I decided, in fact I was saying to myself, there must be a lot of parents who really don't know, they've been out of school for so long they really don't know what goes on in school. And that if they would show a little bit more interest or get in on what's going on they would be able to help their children more. I, as I said before, I had been out of school a very long time and I really had lost track of just what the inside of a school felt like, or looked like, or what was going on. And things have changed quite a bit from the time I went to school to the time Paula went to school. And you walk into the school and you're frightened because it's so different. There is more freedom. And to most parents I suppose this looks like, boy, everything has gone down the drain. But I found out by being involved, a lot of little things that probably wouldn't have occurred to parents whose children are doing, what they say, alright in school, probably if everything is alright I don't have to go in. But one of the things I discovered, Paula came home and she was very happy over the fact that she was in the Glee Club. And I said, oh

great, you know, fine. And then when her report card you know, comes home, in Science, C, and how come? You are so great. Well, you go into school and you find out and I said to the teacher, well she's in the Glee Club. She said, I could care less. She's not in my class. What they do, they get involved in these programs, the Glee Club and the Orchestra and maybe go to the teacher and says, well I got to go to rehearsal, but they're missing out on some of their major subjects. So I told her, I said, now look, all fine and good but you got to rehearse at that Glee Club when you got a free period and not when you're supposed to be having classes. Well, I'm pretty sure that a lot of people don't know this unless they go in and find out.

I also found out that allot of messages between the teacher and the parent never get home and so we had a swinging Parents Association.
